Marco (arch): quick idea — can we try a probe-led approach to tame routing oscillations? we sample short probe requests per route and apply a smoothing/decay to weights instead of immediate hard switches.
Anya (runtime): I like sampling, but how do you avoid probe noise making things worse?
Marco (arch): two parts: 1) use a tiny exponential decay on penalty/bias updates, 2) require a minimum confirmation window (e.g. 3 probe successes/failures across 30s) before flipping a route hard.
Samir (sre): +1 for confirmation window. also need to think about probe traffic cost at high qps — can't probe every tenant-route.
Lina (product): what's the UX for customers when we delay a failover? would they notice extra latency?
Marco (arch): the goal is graceful degrade: we bias rather than preempt immediately. so most traffic continues to low-latency backends while probes validate alternatives. minimize customer-visible blips.
Anya (runtime): implementation choices: sidecar-enforced probes vs central policy compiler that emits probe schedules. Sidecar = faster local reaction, central = consistent global view. tradeoffs?
Samir (sre): sidecars multiply probes by node count — bad. central can rate-limit probes and allocate a global probe budget. but central adds a control-plane roundtrip and potential single point of delayed reaction.
Marco (arch): proposal: hybrid: central compiler emits a probe budget and smoothing params per tenant/route, sidecars run probes but adhere to global budget and report aggregated counters back. avoids explosion and keeps local fast feedback.
Anya (runtime): that fits our telemetry model. need clear contract: probe payloads + latency buckets + success criteria. also require opt-out for sensitive tenants (no synthetic queries).
Samir (sre): telemetry: mark probe metrics with "probe=1" tag and ensure they don't pollute production p95s. also add a separate SLA guardrail that prevents probes from triggering capacity preemptions.
Lina (product): can we do a canary rollout for this? risk-averse customers might want off by default.
Marco (arch): yes — default OFF, opt-in per tenant via policy flag. rollout path: internal -> pilot customers -> broad opt-in via console toggle.
Anya (runtime): corner case: route cache invalidation. if central updates probe budget we must invalidate compatibility caches quickly. suggest a TTL of 10s on probe-related entries and a hotreload hook in the sidecar.
Samir (sre): add a kill-switch in the control plane and an automated rollback playbook if oscillation increases after rollouts. also add an anomaly detector that watches route-churn rate.
Marco (arch): agreed. I'll draft a short RFC: sections = motivation, probe model, smoothing math (alpha decay example), budget contract, telemetry tags, rollout & rollback checklist, compatibility shim.
Anya (runtime): ping me for the smoothing math. quick note on math: use weighted EWMA with variable alpha per tenant qps. low qps => slower alpha.
Lina (product): make sure toggle is visible in Console and API. include recommended defaults.
probe-bot: deploy-bot created a rollout checklist item: `docs/routing/probe-led-rollout.md` in the backlog.
Marco (arch): thanks. action items: Marco write RFC by EOD Wed, Anya draft EWMA snippet, Samir outline monitoring alerts, Lina prepare Console toggle copy. anyone else?
Samir (sre): i'll stub the alert queries and add a dashboard panel for probe-churn.
Anya (runtime): will mock the sidecar budget enforcement API and add a unit test for cache invalidation.
Lina (product): i'll reach out to two pilot customers for approval.
Marco (arch): cool. if we hit surprises we'll fallback to central-only probe scheduling as a safe path.
Samir (sre): :thumbsup:
Lina (product): :ok_hand:
